findings.issue_text: [BUG] Test cleanup calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") for every created IDP, but no IDP with alias "alias" exists, so get() returns null and the method reference null::remove throws NullPointerException during test setup, failing testCacheIDPForLogin. Creating the method reference on a null Resource triggers an immediate NPE at getCleanup().addCleanup(...) (Resource.get on a nonexistent alias returns null), so the test aborts before any cache assertions run and none of the created IDPs are cleaned up.

[BUG] For i >= 10 the test calls idpRep.getConfig().put(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, ...) on a freshly constructed IdentityProviderRepresentation whose config map was never initialized, throwing NullPointerException. IdentityProviderRepresentation.getConfig() returns the null field until setConfig is called; the unguarded .put() NPEs on the first iteration with i >= 10, aborting the test before cache verification.

[BUG] getForLogin() constructs IdentityProviderListQuery with a six-argument constructor (loaded, cacheKey, realm, searchKey, cached, query) and reads cache.getCurrentCounter(), but neither this 6-arg constructor nor a getCurrentCounter() method on RealmCacheManager is added by this diff, so the code does not compile against the repository as changed. The build fails with 'cannot resolve constructor IdentityProviderListQuery(Long, String, RealmModel, String, Set, IdentityProviderListQuery)' / 'cannot resolve method getCurrentCounter()' unless the accompanying storage PR that adds those members is merged first — an unstated prerequisite, so this diff cannot build standalone.

[BUG] The cache key cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) does not include organizationId, so a second getForLogin call with a different organizationId hits the existing query entry whose getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, then unconditionally invalidates the shared cache entry and replaces it — meaning the previously cached organization's result set is evicted on every alternating-organization access. In multi-organization realms (any login page for org A followed by login page for org B), the login cache is invalidated and repopulated on every request, causing a delegate (DB) hit per login page render and defeating the cache the PR exists to add; correctness is preserved only via the always-fresh reload.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate conjunct calls idp.getConfig() unconditionally even when getOrganizationId() is non-null, and IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() can return null for some storage implementations, throwing NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate(). Any caller of getLoginPredicate (e.g. the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation on every IDP create/remove) with a model whose config map is null crashes the write path with NPE instead of skipping the invalidation.

[BUG] The test's cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so all 21 created IDPs are never cleaned up and the cleanup lambda resolves a non-existent resource. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns a null/not-found resource and the ::remove cleanup throws (NPE or 404), failing test teardown and leaking 20+ identity providers (and the org links) into the shared test realm, breaking subsequent tests.

[BUG] The cleanup for the second created IDP ("idp-alias-20") also uses the wrong alias literal "alias". The IDP created at step 1 is never removed, and the cleanup lambda hits a non-existent resource, throwing during cleanup execution.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns IDPs from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (invalid-key at line 218 and the null-idp fallback at line 250) wrap results, so the same call returns organization-aware wrapped models on cache miss and raw unwrapped models on cache hit. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's isEnabled re-check (the diff's own mitigation, added precisely because "idp might have been wrapped") only patches one consumer; any behavior the wrapper changes beyond enabled-state (e.g., alias/config adjustments made by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) diverges between first and subsequent login renders for the same realm, so users see different IDP lists depending on whether the cache was warm.

[ADVISORY] The cache-hit path assembles results into a HashSet and streams it, discarding whatever ordering the delegate (JPA storage) returned for getForLogin. Callers of getForLogin that rely on the delegate's deterministic ordering get nondeterministic ordering on cache hits; the login freemarker bean happens to re-sort, so only non-UI consumers of the SPI are bitten — but the cache layer silently changes a observable property of the result between miss and hit.

[ADVISORY] The fallback branch where a cached IDP id resolves to null (getById returns null -> invalidate cacheKey and reload from delegate) has no test coverage: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises populate/exists/cleared states and never asserts the stale-id recovery path. If the invalidation and reload logic in this branch regresses (e.g., the wrong key is invalidated or the delegate result is returned unwrapped), stale login IDP lists persist indefinitely; a regression here would surface as IDPs appearing on the login page after deletion in a multi-node cluster, and no test in the diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] The isEnabled re-check added to mitigate wrapped IDPs is only applied to the ORG_ONLY-with-no-org path and the final ALL/organization path, but no test in the diff verifies that a wrapped, disabled IDP is actually excluded from the login page via this new filter. The test suite never constructs the wrapped-disabled-IDP scenario this re-check exists for, so if the re-check is dropped or inverted in a refactor, the bug it papers over (disabled IDPs rendered on the organization login page when the cache layer returns differently-wrapped models) silently returns.

[BUG] The cache-hit path in getForLogin returns raw delegate models without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same call returns different model types/behavior depending on whether the cache is warm. First call (cache miss / invalid) wraps org-linked IDPs in organization-aware models, but every subsequent cached call skips the wrapping entirely; any consumer relying on the org-aware wrapper behavior (e.g., the login page IDP bean) silently gets divergent results on the second and later requests within the cache lifetime.

[ADVISORY] The PR changes getLoginPredicate() in the shared SPI, altering the visible filtering semantics of getLoginPredicate for every caller and every storage provider (including non-cached JPA deployments), which is behavior drift beyond the stated 'add caching' intent. Deployments without the infinispan cache (cache=disabled) get a changed set of login-eligible IDPs (org-linked non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs now excluded) from this PR without any requirement or test covering the non-cached path, and any other caller of getLoginPredicate (e.g. mapIdentityProviders or third-party storage providers) inherits the new predicate silently.

[ADVISORY] The chained-query retry path uses cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision for addRevisioned while the initial population uses startupRevision, an inconsistency not traceable to any requirement and not exercised by the new test. The new test (testCacheIDPForLogin) only covers one organizationId per FetchMode, so the second-distinct-org branch (invalidateObject + re-add with getCurrentCounter) ships with zero coverage; a revision-handling mistake there would only surface in production multi-org realms.

[BUG] The test cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove for every created IDP, referencing a nonexistent alias "alias" instead of the actual aliases "idp-alias-" + i. The cleanup lambda resolves the wrong resource (returns null / removes nothing for alias 'alias'), so the 21 created IDPs leak across the test realm and can corrupt the counts asserted by later cache assertions in the same class.

[ADVISORY] update() computes registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate against idpById obtained via getById(model.getInternalId()), which for the new predicate depends on the organization link that getById (a cached read) may serve stale, making the skip-invalidation optimization only as trustworthy as the per-IDP cache it just read. If the alias/internalId entity cache is stale or the internalId lookup misses (idpById null), the update-invalidates-nothing branch (NPE risk when getLoginPredicate().test(null) evaluates idp.getConfig()) or wrongly skips invalidation, leaving stale login lists cluster-wide; the test never exercises the idpById == null path.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from getById with no createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, while the cache-miss path (line 213) wraps every result, so the same method returns different model types depending on cache state. A login-page request served from the cache receives non-organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances while an identical request after invalidation receives wrapped ones; any consumer relying on the wrapper's behavior (this is exactly why OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean in this diff had to bolt on a re-check of isEnabled() 'as idp might have been wrapped') silently gets different results for the same query, and the isEnabled() re-filter in the bean is a symptom-masking patch rather than the fix.

[BUG] The LoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, and the short-circuit only protects the orgId==null case. Any IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set and a null config (a state the model API permits — config is a plain settable field) throws NPE when getLoginPredicate().test(idp) runs, which now executes on every getForLogin call, every create() and every update() through the cache provider, turning a login-page render into a 500.

[ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate() change is a global semantic change to the IdentityProviderStorageProvider SPI, not a cache-local one: non-public org-linked IDPs are now excluded from getForLogin for every storage implementation, including ORG_ONLY fetches. Users of organization-scoped login (FetchMode.ORG_ONLY) whose orgs have broker-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC=true lose those IDPs from the organization login page on every storage provider, not just the cached one — a behavior change to a documented SPI method shipped inside a 'add caching support' PR; if the intent was only to make cached results deterministic, the filter belongs in the cache layer, not in the shared predicate.

[ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revision bases: the first addRevisioned call passes startupRevision while the second passes cache.getCurrentCounter() after an explicit invalidateObject(cacheKey), unlike the sibling keys (idp.alias, idp.orgId) which consistently use the revision obtained after invalidation. A search for a second organizationId in the same FetchMode takes the second branch; if the revision/counter mismatch causes addRevisioned to bail or the entry to be compared against a stale revision, the org-specific result set is silently dropped and every request for that org re-runs the delegate query and rewrites the cache entry, negating the cache for all orgs except the most recently searched one — the exact class of revision asymmetry the existing cached-query code was written to avoid.

[ADVISORY] update() derives its invalidation decision from idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()), which is served through the cache, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the updated model against a possibly-stale cached original rather than the persisted state. When a prior update on another node has not yet propagated the invalidation, the cached 'original' can match the updated model on all predicate-relevant fields (enabled, hideOnLogin, org link), so the update skips invalidating the login cache keys even though the stored row actually changed login eligibility — cluster-wide stale login IDP lists until the cache entry expires by revision; the invalidation decision should be computed from the delegate (source of truth), as the alias-invalidation path in the same method already risks.

[BUG] The cleanup registration is `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, but no IDP with alias "alias" exists — every created IDP has alias "idp-alias-<i>" — so get("alias") returns null and the method reference creation throws NPE (or the cleanup silently no-ops), leaving 21 test IDPs in the realm. Each of the ~22 cleanup registrations is broken; the test leaks identity providers into the shared test realm, causing cross-test pollution in OrganizationCacheTest and related suite tests.

[BUG] This PR, titled as pure caching support for getForLogin, silently changes the semantics of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() for every implementation and caller (cached and uncached alike) by excluding any org-linked IdP that lacks OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC in its config. Org-linked identity providers not explicitly marked BROKER_PUBLIC silently disappear from organization login pages (getForLogin results) on every code path, including deployments with the realm cache disabled and non-Infinispan storage providers — a behavior change in the login flow shipped under a caching PR with no independent flagging or migration note; operators who linked broker IdPs to orgs without setting brokerPublic will lose those login buttons after upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' documents that the cached getForLogin path can return wrapped organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances whose enabled flag is not honored by the login predicate, so the bean compensates downstream. Any other consumer of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin (third-party or future callers of the SPI) that does not duplicate the isEnabled() re-check will render disabled IdPs from the cache; the filtering contract has drifted from the storage provider to individual callers.

[BUG] The 'search key not yet cached' branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of the startupRevision used by every other addRevisioned call in this class, so the freshly built IdentityProviderListQuery is registered against a revision the cache logic does not treat as the session's startup revision. When multiple organizationId searches interleave against the same FetchMode cache key, the query created with getCurrentCounter can cause subsequent cache.get lookups to miss or to resurrect stale IdP lists, returning wrong IdPs on the org-scoped login page.

[BUG] The new predicate term calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null check on getConfig(), throwing NullPointerException for any IdentityProviderModel whose config map is null while having a non-null organizationId. An IDP created/loaded with organizationId set but a null config map (config is nullable in IdentityProviderModel) makes getLoginPredicate() throw during login-page IDP resolution, breaking the realm's login flow (500 on the login page / broken broker listing) rather than merely excluding the IDP.

[ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is only triggered from create/update/remove on this provider, but organization-to-IDP link changes that flow through OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider without a subsequent provider-visible update leave the cached login ID lists stale. An admin unlinks a broker from an organization (or toggles its org link) via org-management endpoints that bypass this provider's update path; users on the login page continue to see the stale cached IDP (or miss a newly public one) until an unrelated invalidation occurs — a stale-authorization-style exposure where the login surface shows brokers the operator removed.

[BUG] The cleanup registration for the created IDPs uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20 providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are never removed by cleanup. After the test runs, 20 identity providers (10 linked to the organization) leak into the shared test realm; subsequent tests that enumerate realm IDPs or organization IDPs see unexpected brokers, causing cross-test pollution and flaky failures in whatever test runs next against this realm.

[BUG] The second cleanup registration repeats the wrong literal alias ("idp-alias-20" is created but cleanup targets alias "alias"), so this IDP is also leaked. The idp-alias-20 provider created mid-test survives cleanup, polluting the shared test realm for subsequent tests just like the loop-created providers.

[ADVISORY] The test discards the return value of every session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) call and only asserts on the internal IdentityProviderListQuery cache entry, so it never verifies that getForLogin actually returns the correct IdentityProviderModel set. If getForLogin's reconstruction loop returns wrong, duplicate, or organization-unaware models (e.g. the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel mapping is broken or returns an empty set from the cache while the cache entry is populated correctly), the test still passes — a false-confidence test that verifies cache bookkeeping, not the feature's user-visible behavior.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate branch in getLoginPredicate (excluding organization-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC) is never exercised negatively — every org-linked IDP in testCacheIDPForLogin (idp-alias-10..19 and idp-alias-20 in step 4) sets OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true, so no test ever creates an org-linked, non-public IDP and asserts it is excluded from login results. This is a behavior change affecting all IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations (not just the cache): a realm-level admin linking an IDP to an organization without marking it public now silently disappears from the login page. The excluded-branch can regress (or mask an off-by-one in which public ones are also excluded) without any test failing; I checked OrganizationCacheTest.java, the only test file in the diff, and it contains no non-public org-linked IDP scenario.

[ADVISORY] The fallback branch in getForLogin where a cached internal ID resolves to null (realmCache.registerInvalidation + delegate re-fetch) is never triggered by any test — the diff's only test (OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin) never invalidates an individual IDP while its login list-query remains valid. If this branch has a bug (wrong invalidation key, missing map to organization-aware model, or returning a stream built from a session whose cache was just invalidated mid-iteration), stale or empty login IDP lists would be served in production after an IDP is removed out-of-band; the test suite gives no signal because no test drives a cached-hit-with-missing-IDP state.

[ADVISORY] The 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not cached' branch — including the addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) call that differs from the first-branch's startupRevision argument — is never executed by testCacheIDPForLogin, which calls getForLogin exactly once per (mode, searchKey) pair. A second organization (or switching the same mode between null and an orgId) takes the untested append branch; if addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter misbehaves (revision mismatch causing the query to be dropped or to overwrite the prior searchKey), multi-organization realms get missing IDP lists in production with zero test coverage; the suite never calls getForLogin twice against the same mode key.

[ADVISORY] The new idp.isEnabled() re-check filter (added because cached/wrapped IDPs may lose their enabled state) is a behavioral change in the login-page IDP listing with no test in this diff that exercises OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or the wrapped-model scenario the comment describes. The stated failure mode — a cached or organization-aware wrapped IdentityProviderModel reporting isEnabled()=false appearing on (or disappearing from) the login page — is precisely the scenario the new filter guards, yet no test in OrganizationCacheTest (the only test file changed) ever asserts the rendered login IDP list or the bean's filter behavior; a regression reintroducing or mishandling the filter passes the suite. I checked OrganizationCacheTest.java — it contains no reference to OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or any login-page assertion.

[BUG] getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on the config map, NPE-ing for any organization-linked IdentityProviderModel whose config is null. An org-linked IDP deserialized from the Infinispan cache or constructed by an extension with a null config map makes getLoginPredicate throw NullPointerException; in the cache provider this NPE fires inside create()/update()/remove() via registerIDPLoginInvalidation, breaking IDP management operations, and inside getForLogin, breaking the login page with a 500.

[ADVISORY] This PR is titled as caching support, but the getLoginPredicate change silently reclassifies every existing org-linked, non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC absent/false) IDP out of the login set for all providers, including the non-cached JPA path. Realms upgrading to this version see org-linked broker IdPs disappear from org login pages (orgs that relied on members-only brokers appearing) with no migration note, feature flag, or changelog entry; the change is shipped inside a 'caching' PR and reviewers/users will not expect a behavior change to login semantics.

[ADVISORY] When a cached IdentityProviderListQuery exists but lacks the current searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then addRevisioned with cache.getCurrentCounter(), which other cluster nodes can race with: a node that already fetched the old query between the invalidateObject and the addRevisioned re-caches against a stale snapshot, and the update-time invalidation skip (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returning early) then leaves the org-scoped stale list in place. In a multi-node cluster, a login-IDP update that the skip condition considers non-invalidation-worthy (e.g. alias-only change) coinciding with an org-scoped cache expansion can serve a stale org login list to users until some other operation invalidates the key; single-node tests like testCacheIDPForLogin cannot exercise this window.

[BUG] On a cache hit the cached IDPs from session.identityProviders().getById(id) bypass createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (the initial load and the idp == null fallback) run the models through that wrapper, producing different IdentityProviderModel instances/behavior for the same login-page request depending on whether the login cache is warm. The very existence of the re-added `idp.isEnabled()` filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (comment: "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped") shows wrapped models diverge from raw ones; on cache hits the login page renders unwrapped cached models, so attributes the wrapper is supposed to contribute (organization-aware alias/config) silently differ between cache-miss and cache-hit renders, and the bean-level re-check only patches one of the divergences.

[BUG] The second-population branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) while the first-population branch uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), so the guard against installing a query over a concurrently-invalidated cache entry is bypassed in the multi-organization case. When one request is populating the cache for a second organizationId at the same moment another node/session invalidates the login cache (e.g. an IDP update), addRevisioned succeeds with a non-startup revision and stores a query built from pre-invalidation data, resurrecting stale login-IDP lists that the invalidation was supposed to clear; users see removed/disabled IDPs on the login page.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before the cache-lookup branch, adding a guaranteed delegate (DB) read on every IDP removal even when the cache already holds the entry that used to satisfy the lookup. Every identity-provider removal across all realms pays an extra storage hit on a write path that previously could be served from cache; operators running hot IDP admin traffic see added DB load for information the cache branch already retrieves via the cached value.

[ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is registered only from IDP create/update/remove in this provider; organization lifecycle changes that alter getForLogin results (organization removal unlinking IDPs, disabling an organization) do not register cacheKeyForLogin invalidations here, and the new login predicate's dependence on organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC makes those results sensitive to org-state. After an admin deletes or disables an organization whose linked public IDPs are cached in a login list query, login pages in that realm keep showing the stale org-linked IDPs until some unrelated IDP write triggers invalidation, letting users attempt brokering through a removed organization's IDP.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate clause idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) calls idp.getConfig() without a null guard, and applies the public check uniformly to all FetchMode values including ORG_ONLY, where members of the organization are expected to also see non-public broker entries. Any IdentityProviderModel implementation or deserialization path that leaves config null (getConfig() returning null) makes the shared getLoginPredicate throw NPE on every getForLogin call, breaking the login page; and org members lose their non-public organization brokers from the login page because ORG_ONLY results are filtered to public-only entries, contradicting the members-see-all-org-brokers behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce calls to `new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, cacheKey, getRealm(), searchKey, cached, query)` and `cache.getCurrentCounter()` inside `getForLogin()`. However, this PR diff does not show the definition of `IdentityProviderListQuery` or `RealmCacheManager`, so it is not verifiable from the diff alone that the 6-arg constructor and `getCurrentCounter()` are missing in the repository state. They may already exist outside the shown changes, so the claim that the code "does not compile" cannot be confirmed solely from this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the cache entry key is per (realm, FetchMode), but the cached IdentityProviderListQuery is explicitly designed to hold multiple result sets keyed by a per-request `searchKey` (`organizationId` or ""). The code only invalidates `cacheKey` when `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns null (i.e., that org hasn’t been cached yet), then rebuilds the query and passes the previous `query` into the constructor (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)`), which is presumably meant to retain previously cached org result sets. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that alternating between org A and org B will evict the other org “on every request”; once both orgs are present in the query, `getIDPs(searchKey)` should be non-null and no invalidation/reload occurs.

This is a concrete robustness/edge-case concern because callers added in this PR (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`) now invoke this predicate on create/update/remove. However, the diff does not show whether `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null across implementations, so an actual NPE crash cannot be verified solely from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin(), the cleanup registration after creating IDPs uses `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (both in the initial loop and again after creating "idp-alias-20"). This hard-coded literal "alias" does not match the created aliases (e.g., "idp-alias-20"), so the created IDP(s) are not removed and the cleanup will attempt to remove a non-existent IDP resource, likely failing during cleanup execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns IDPs from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (invalid-key at line 218 and the null-idp fallback at line 250) wrap results, so the same call returns organization-aware wrapped models on cache miss and raw unwrapped models on cache hit. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's isEnabled re-check (the diff's own mitigation, added precisely because "idp might have been wrapped") only patches one consumer; any behavior the wrapper changes beyond enabled-state (e.g., alias/config adjustments made by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) diverges between first and subsequent login renders for the same realm, so users see different IDP lists depending on whether the cache was warm.

adjudication.rationale: In the new InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (lines around 213), and the null-idp fallback also returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (around 249). However, on the cache-hit path it reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes the same API return wrapped (organization-aware) models on miss/fallback but raw models on hit, which can change downstream behavior and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-hit path assembles results into a HashSet and streams it, discarding whatever ordering the delegate (JPA storage) returned for getForLogin. Callers of getForLogin that rely on the delegate's deterministic ordering get nondeterministic ordering on cache hits; the login freemarker bean happens to re-sort, so only non-UI consumers of the SPI are bitten — but the cache layer silently changes a observable property of the result between miss and hit.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cache-hit path for `getForLogin`, results are accumulated into `Set<IdentityProviderModel> identityProviders = new HashSet<>()` and returned via `identityProviders.stream()` (and the cached IDs are also stored/loaded as a `Set<String>`). This loses any ordering that the delegate stream might have had on a cache miss, so cache hits can yield nondeterministic iteration order vs misses. Whether ordering is contractually required isn’t shown in the diff, but the diff does introduce an observable ordering difference between miss and hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fallback branch where a cached IDP id resolves to null (getById returns null -> invalidate cacheKey and reload from delegate) has no test coverage: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises populate/exists/cleared states and never asserts the stale-id recovery path. If the invalidation and reload logic in this branch regresses (e.g., the wrong key is invalidated or the delegate result is returned unwrapped), stale login IDP lists persist indefinitely; a regression here would surface as IDPs appearing on the login page after deletion in a multi-node cluster, and no test in the diff would catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The new caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` includes a specific stale-entry recovery path: when iterating cached internal IDs, `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` may return `null`, and the code then calls `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`. The added `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on create/update/remove, but it never sets up a scenario where a cached ID refers to a deleted/missing IDP such that `getById` returns `null`, so that recovery branch is indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The isEnabled re-check added to mitigate wrapped IDPs is only applied to the ORG_ONLY-with-no-org path and the final ALL/organization path, but no test in the diff verifies that a wrapped, disabled IDP is actually excluded from the login page via this new filter. The test suite never constructs the wrapped-disabled-IDP scenario this re-check exists for, so if the re-check is dropped or inverted in a refactor, the bug it papers over (disabled IDPs rendered on the organization login page when the cache layer returns differently-wrapped models) silently returns.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new defensive filtering in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean: both login-IDP query paths now apply `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` with a comment about wrapped IDPs potentially bypassing the original enabled filtering. The newly added test (testCacheIDPForLogin) exercises getForLogin caching/invalidation and enabled/disabled IDPs at the storage layer, but it never goes through OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean nor constructs/validates the specific “wrapped but disabled IDP still appearing” scenario that motivated the re-check. So the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap concern, not a demonstrated functional defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path in getForLogin returns raw delegate models without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same call returns different model types/behavior depending on whether the cache is warm. First call (cache miss / invalid) wraps org-linked IDPs in organization-aware models, but every subsequent cached call skips the wrapping entirely; any consumer relying on the org-aware wrapper behavior (e.g., the login page IDP bean) silently gets divergent results on the second and later requests within the cache lifetime.

adjudication.rationale: In the cache-hit branch of `getForLogin`, the code does not explicitly call `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, but it also does not return the delegate’s raw results: it resolves each IDP via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`. From this diff alone we cannot verify what `getById` returns (it may already apply `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` internally), so the claim that warm-cache calls "skip the wrapping entirely" and return different model types/behavior is not provable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR changes getLoginPredicate() in the shared SPI, altering the visible filtering semantics of getLoginPredicate for every caller and every storage provider (including non-cached JPA deployments), which is behavior drift beyond the stated 'add caching' intent. Deployments without the infinispan cache (cache=disabled) get a changed set of login-eligible IDPs (org-linked non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs now excluded) from this PR without any requirement or test covering the non-cached path, and any other caller of getLoginPredicate (e.g. mapIdentityProviders or third-party storage providers) inherits the new predicate silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change shared SPI behavior: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` gains an additional constraint `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will affect every caller of `getLoginPredicate()` and thus the results of `getForLogin(...)` across all storage providers (not just the new Infinispan caching path). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises only the Infinispan cache behavior via `RealmCacheSession` and does not cover the non-cached path, so the review concern about broader, silent semantic drift from an SPI change is grounded in the diff (even if the new semantics might be intended).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The chained-query retry path uses cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision for addRevisioned while the initial population uses startupRevision, an inconsistency not traceable to any requirement and not exercised by the new test. The new test (testCacheIDPForLogin) only covers one organizationId per FetchMode, so the second-distinct-org branch (invalidateObject + re-add with getCurrentCounter) ships with zero coverage; a revision-handling mistake there would only surface in production multi-org realms.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new caching path in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`. In the initial population (`query == null`), it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but in the “second searchKey not yet cached” branch (`cached == null` after `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`), it does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This revision-source mismatch is directly present in the diff and could affect cache revision semantics, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s incorrect. The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only exercises one `organizationId` per `FetchMode`, so it never hits the `cached == null` branch (which requires a second distinct `organizationId`/searchKey for the same `FetchMode`), leaving that new logic untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove for every created IDP, referencing a nonexistent alias "alias" instead of the actual aliases "idp-alias-" + i. The cleanup lambda resolves the wrong resource (returns null / removes nothing for alias 'alias'), so the 21 created IDPs leak across the test realm and can corrupt the counts asserted by later cache assertions in the same class.

[ADVISORY] update() computes registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate against idpById obtained via getById(model.getInternalId()), which for the new predicate depends on the organization link that getById (a cached read) may serve stale, making the skip-invalidation optimization only as trustworthy as the per-IDP cache it just read. If the alias/internalId entity cache is stale or the internalId lookup misses (idpById null), the update-invalidates-nothing branch (NPE risk when getLoginPredicate().test(null) evaluates idp.getConfig()) or wrongly skips invalidation, leaving stale login lists cluster-wide; the test never exercises the idpById == null path.

adjudication.rationale:
The finding’s concrete NPE claim is contradicted by the diff: `getLoginPredicate()` is built as `((Predicate<IdentityProviderModel>) Objects::nonNull).and(...)`, so `getLoginPredicate().test(null)` short-circuits on `Objects::nonNull` and will not evaluate `idp.getOrganizationId()`/`idp.getConfig()`.

The other claim (that `getById()` is a “cached read” that may be stale, making the skip-invalidation optimization unreliable cluster-wide) is not verifiable from the shown diff because the implementation/consistency guarantees of `getById()` and the cache invalidation mechanism are not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from getById with no createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, while the cache-miss path (line 213) wraps every result, so the same method returns different model types depending on cache state. A login-page request served from the cache receives non-organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances while an identical request after invalidation receives wrapped ones; any consumer relying on the wrapper's behavior (this is exactly why OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean in this diff had to bolt on a re-check of isEnabled() 'as idp might have been wrapped') silently gets different results for the same query, and the isEnabled() re-filter in the bean is a symptom-masking patch rather than the fix.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss/invalid path explicitly wraps results via `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path builds the result set by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns those models directly with no corresponding `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping. From the diff alone, this means the method can return differently wrapped model instances depending on cache state, which is observable behavior and matches the concern raised (the bean change comment also hints at inconsistent wrapping).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The LoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, and the short-circuit only protects the orgId==null case. Any IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set and a null config (a state the model API permits — config is a plain settable field) throws NPE when getLoginPredicate().test(idp) runs, which now executes on every getForLogin call, every create() and every update() through the cache provider, turning a login-page render into a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to call `idp.getConfig().get(...)` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null` (the `||` only short-circuits the orgId==null case). There is no null-guard for `getConfig()` in the predicate, so an NPE is possible if `getConfig()` can be null. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish that `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` may be null in practice (model/API not shown), so the claim that this is a definite, newly-triggered 500 cannot be fully verified from the PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate() change is a global semantic change to the IdentityProviderStorageProvider SPI, not a cache-local one: non-public org-linked IDPs are now excluded from getForLogin for every storage implementation, including ORG_ONLY fetches. Users of organization-scoped login (FetchMode.ORG_ONLY) whose orgs have broker-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC=true lose those IDPs from the organization login page on every storage provider, not just the cached one — a behavior change to a documented SPI method shipped inside a 'add caching support' PR; if the intent was only to make cached results deterministic, the filter belongs in the cache layer, not in the shared predicate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` in `server-spi` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. Because this predicate lives in the SPI (not the Infinispan cache provider), it can affect `getForLogin(...)` behavior anywhere that predicate is used, across all storage implementations, not just caching. This is a scope/architecture concern: a PR primarily adding caching also introduces a cross-provider semantic filter on org-linked IDPs based on `BROKER_PUBLIC`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revision bases: the first addRevisioned call passes startupRevision while the second passes cache.getCurrentCounter() after an explicit invalidateObject(cacheKey), unlike the sibling keys (idp.alias, idp.orgId) which consistently use the revision obtained after invalidation. A search for a second organizationId in the same FetchMode takes the second branch; if the revision/counter mismatch causes addRevisioned to bail or the entry to be compared against a stale revision, the org-specific result set is silently dropped and every request for that org re-runs the delegate query and rewrites the cache entry, negating the cache for all orgs except the most recently searched one — the exact class of revision asymmetry the existing cached-query code was written to avoid.

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin() caching logic, the two cache-population paths do use different revision values when writing the query: when query == null it calls cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), but when extending the cached query for a new searchKey (cached == null) it explicitly invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded, and it’s reasonable to flag because revision/counter handling is central to the cache’s correctness/performance. However, the specific failure mode described (addRevisioned bailing or silently dropping org-specific results) depends on the undocumented semantics of addRevisioned/getCurrentRevision/getCurrentCounter, which are not shown in the diff, so it can’t be verified as an actual defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update() derives its invalidation decision from idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()), which is served through the cache, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the updated model against a possibly-stale cached original rather than the persisted state. When a prior update on another node has not yet propagated the invalidation, the cached 'original' can match the updated model on all predicate-relevant fields (enabled, hideOnLogin, org link), so the update skips invalidating the login cache keys even though the stored row actually changed login eligibility — cluster-wide stale login IDP lists until the cache entry expires by revision; the invalidation decision should be computed from the delegate (source of truth), as the alias-invalidation path in the same method already risks.

adjudication.rationale: In update(), the code obtains the "original" model via getById(model.getInternalId()) and then uses that value to decide whether to invalidate the new login caches (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model)). Given this class is a cache-backed provider and the method does not explicitly bypass cache to consult idpDelegate, the invalidation decision is potentially based on cached state rather than the current persisted state. The added early-return logic in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate (skipping invalidation when predicate-relevant fields appear unchanged) can therefore skip invalidating cacheKeyForLogin(...) entries if the cached original matches the updated model even though the underlying stored IDP changed eligibility elsewhere, leaving stale cached login IDP lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration is `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, but no IDP with alias "alias" exists — every created IDP has alias "idp-alias-<i>" — so get("alias") returns null and the method reference creation throws NPE (or the cleanup silently no-ops), leaving 21 test IDPs in the realm. Each of the ~22 cleanup registrations is broken; the test leaks identity providers into the shared test realm, causing cross-test pollution in OrganizationCacheTest and related suite tests.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the loop creates IDPs with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i`, but registers cleanup via `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias"). The diff shows no IDP created with alias "alias", so `identityProviders().get("alias")` will return null and the method reference will fail (or the cleanup will not remove the created IDPs), leaking test data and risking cross-test pollution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This PR, titled as pure caching support for getForLogin, silently changes the semantics of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() for every implementation and caller (cached and uncached alike) by excluding any org-linked IdP that lacks OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC in its config. Org-linked identity providers not explicitly marked BROKER_PUBLIC silently disappear from organization login pages (getForLogin results) on every code path, including deployments with the realm cache disabled and non-Infinispan storage providers — a behavior change in the login flow shipped under a caching PR with no independent flagging or migration note; operators who linked broker IdPs to orgs without setting brokerPublic will lose those login buttons after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the global semantics of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` (server-spi). This will exclude any org-linked IdP whose config lacks/has false `BROKER_PUBLIC` across all implementations and callers (cached or not), not just the new Infinispan caching path. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this new exclusion is *incorrect* (the added integration test constructs org-linked IdPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` and asserts those results), so it’s best characterized as a scope/behavior-change concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' documents that the cached getForLogin path can return wrapped organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances whose enabled flag is not honored by the login predicate, so the bean compensates downstream. Any other consumer of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin (third-party or future callers of the SPI) that does not duplicate the isEnabled() re-check will render disabled IdPs from the cache; the filtering contract has drifted from the storage provider to individual callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching for `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` and adds a defensive `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() ...)` in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, but the diff does not show that the cached `getForLogin` path actually returns disabled IDPs. The cached ID set is populated from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, and cache invalidation on update is driven by `getLoginPredicate()` via `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)`, which is intended to invalidate when login-eligibility changes (including enabled/hidden if those are part of `LoginFilter`’s filters, not shown here). The finding’s claim that the enabled flag is “not honored by the login predicate” and that other callers will render disabled IDPs from cache is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'search key not yet cached' branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of the startupRevision used by every other addRevisioned call in this class, so the freshly built IdentityProviderListQuery is registered against a revision the cache logic does not treat as the session's startup revision. When multiple organizationId searches interleave against the same FetchMode cache key, the query created with getCurrentCounter can cause subsequent cache.get lookups to miss or to resurrect stale IdP lists, returning wrong IdPs on the org-scoped login page.

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the first-time cache population path uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but the "searchKey not yet cached" path invalidates the object and then uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and could indicate a revisioning/consistency issue in how the cache entry is registered. However, the finding’s specific behavioral claim (misses/resurrecting stale IdP lists due to startup-revision semantics under interleaving org searches) is not verifiable from this diff alone because the revisioning contract of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, and `getCurrentCounter()` isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate term calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null check on getConfig(), throwing NullPointerException for any IdentityProviderModel whose config map is null while having a non-null organizationId. An IDP created/loaded with organizationId set but a null config map (config is nullable in IdentityProviderModel) makes getLoginPredicate() throw during login-page IDP resolution, breaking the realm's login flow (500 on the login page / broken broker listing) rather than merely excluding the IDP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new login predicate term: `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. It indeed dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check when `organizationId != null`, so an NPE would occur if `getConfig()` can return null. However, the diff does not show the `IdentityProviderModel` contract or any code proving `getConfig()` is nullable / can be null in practice, so a definite, verifiable defect cannot be concluded from the diff alone; it is a concrete edge-case risk tied to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is only triggered from create/update/remove on this provider, but organization-to-IDP link changes that flow through OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider without a subsequent provider-visible update leave the cached login ID lists stale. An admin unlinks a broker from an organization (or toggles its org link) via org-management endpoints that bypass this provider's update path; users on the login page continue to see the stale cached IDP (or miss a newly public one) until an unrelated invalidation occurs — a stale-authorization-style exposure where the login surface shows brokers the operator removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds login-list caching in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` and invalidates those caches on `create`, `update` (including when `getOrganizationId()` changes), and `remove`. The finding asserts org↔IDP link changes bypass this provider and thus leave the new login caches stale, but the diff does not show how `OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider` is implemented or whether it triggers an IDP update/invalidation. In fact, the newly added `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` explicitly performs `organizations().identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...)` after caches are populated and asserts the login caches are cleared, implying the link operation *does* result in invalidation (directly or indirectly). Therefore the claimed bypass/staleness is not verifiable from this diff and is contradicted by the added test expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration for the created IDPs uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20 providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are never removed by cleanup. After the test runs, 20 identity providers (10 linked to the organization) leak into the shared test realm; subsequent tests that enumerate realm IDPs or organization IDPs see unexpected brokers, causing cross-test pollution and flaky failures in whatever test runs next against this realm.
matched_golden_ids: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly states that cleanup uses the literal alias "alias" instead of constructing "idp-alias-" + i, which is exactly the golden comment’s underlying bug about incorrect alias usage during cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second cleanup registration repeats the wrong literal alias ("idp-alias-20" is created but cleanup targets alias "alias"), so this IDP is also leaked. The idp-alias-20 provider created mid-test survives cleanup, polluting the shared test realm for subsequent tests just like the loop-created providers.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup registrations use `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` both in the initial creation loop and again after creating `idp-alias-20`. This literal "alias" does not match the created provider aliases (e.g., `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19`, `idp-alias-20`), so those IDPs would not be removed by cleanup, leaking into the shared test realm and potentially polluting subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test discards the return value of every session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) call and only asserts on the internal IdentityProviderListQuery cache entry, so it never verifies that getForLogin actually returns the correct IdentityProviderModel set. If getForLogin's reconstruction loop returns wrong, duplicate, or organization-unaware models (e.g. the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel mapping is broken or returns an empty set from the cache while the cache entry is populated correctly), the test still passes — a false-confidence test that verifies cache bookkeeping, not the feature's user-visible behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In testCacheIDPForLogin, each call to session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) discards the returned Stream and the assertions only inspect the internal IdentityProviderListQuery cached under cacheKeyForLogin(...). The test therefore validates cache population/invalidations and cached ID sets (via getIDPs(searchKey).size()), but never asserts that the public API actually returns the expected IdentityProviderModel instances (e.g., that the reconstruction loop over cached IDs returns the right models, without duplicates, and with organization-aware wrapping via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel). This is a concrete coverage gap for the newly added getForLogin caching/reconstruction logic, not a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate branch in getLoginPredicate (excluding organization-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC) is never exercised negatively — every org-linked IDP in testCacheIDPForLogin (idp-alias-10..19 and idp-alias-20 in step 4) sets OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true, so no test ever creates an org-linked, non-public IDP and asserts it is excluded from login results. This is a behavior change affecting all IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations (not just the cache): a realm-level admin linking an IDP to an organization without marking it public now silently disappears from the login page. The excluded-branch can regress (or mask an off-by-one in which public ones are also excluded) without any test failing; I checked OrganizationCacheTest.java, the only test file in the diff, and it contains no non-public org-linked IDP scenario.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a new condition to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` requiring `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. The only added/modified test in the diff (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) creates org-linked IDPs (aliases 10–19 and later alias 20) but always sets `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` for any IDP that gets linked to an organization. There is no scenario creating an org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` absent/false and asserting it is excluded from `getForLogin(...)` results, so the new negative branch is not exercised by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fallback branch in getForLogin where a cached internal ID resolves to null (realmCache.registerInvalidation + delegate re-fetch) is never triggered by any test — the diff's only test (OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin) never invalidates an individual IDP while its login list-query remains valid. If this branch has a bug (wrong invalidation key, missing map to organization-aware model, or returning a stream built from a session whose cache was just invalidated mid-iteration), stale or empty login IDP lists would be served in production after an IDP is removed out-of-band; the test suite gives no signal because no test drives a cached-hit-with-missing-IDP state.

adjudication.rationale: The new getForLogin caching logic in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider has an explicit fallback when iterating cached internal IDs: if session.identityProviders().getById(id) returns null, it calls realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey) and re-fetches from idpDelegate (mapped to createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel). In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin, the test populates the login caches and then performs operations that either (a) affect IDPs that do not qualify for login (e.g., removing idp-alias-1 which is disabled, and creating idp-alias-20 with hideOnLogin=true) or (b) invalidate the whole login cache on purpose (by changing hideOnLogin / org linkage). It never creates the specific state where the login list-query cache entry remains valid but contains an internalId that no longer resolves (i.e., cached-hit-with-missing-IDP), so that fallback branch is indeed unexercised by the added test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not cached' branch — including the addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) call that differs from the first-branch's startupRevision argument — is never executed by testCacheIDPForLogin, which calls getForLogin exactly once per (mode, searchKey) pair. A second organization (or switching the same mode between null and an orgId) takes the untested append branch; if addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter misbehaves (revision mismatch causing the query to be dropped or to overwrite the prior searchKey), multi-organization realms get missing IDP lists in production with zero test coverage; the suite never calls getForLogin twice against the same mode key.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the branch `if (query != null) { cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { ... cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey); ... query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query); cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()); } }` is only reached when the same `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` already exists but a new `searchKey` (organizationId vs "") is requested. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` calls `getForLogin` at most once per (FetchMode, searchKey) before caches are invalidated/cleared (it never switches the same mode between null and an orgId, nor uses a second orgId while the cache entry remains), so this append/merge path and its differing `addRevisioned(..., cache.getCurrentCounter())` behavior is not exercised. This is a specific coverage gap for newly added caching logic, not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new idp.isEnabled() re-check filter (added because cached/wrapped IDPs may lose their enabled state) is a behavioral change in the login-page IDP listing with no test in this diff that exercises OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or the wrapped-model scenario the comment describes. The stated failure mode — a cached or organization-aware wrapped IdentityProviderModel reporting isEnabled()=false appearing on (or disappearing from) the login page — is precisely the scenario the new filter guards, yet no test in OrganizationCacheTest (the only test file changed) ever asserts the rendered login IDP list or the bean's filter behavior; a regression reintroducing or mishandling the filter passes the suite. I checked OrganizationCacheTest.java — it contains no reference to OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or any login-page assertion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavioral filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)`: `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` (twice), justified by a comment about wrapped/cached IDPs possibly needing an `isEnabled()` re-check. The only test added/modified is `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, which exercises caching via `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and asserts cache contents (`IdentityProviderListQuery` sizes), but does not reference `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, does not render/assert the login-page IDP list, and does not validate the new `isEnabled()` filter behavior. Therefore, the finding that this nontrivial UI-listing behavior change lacks a direct test in this diff is accurate and specific to the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on the config map, NPE-ing for any organization-linked IdentityProviderModel whose config is null. An org-linked IDP deserialized from the Infinispan cache or constructed by an extension with a null config map makes getLoginPredicate throw NullPointerException; in the cache provider this NPE fires inside create()/update()/remove() via registerIDPLoginInvalidation, breaking IDP management operations, and inside getForLogin, breaking the login page with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), the new predicate `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without any null guard. Because this is only short-circuited when `getOrganizationId() == null`, any org-linked `IdentityProviderModel` with a null config map would throw `NullPointerException` during `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`. This predicate is invoked by the new cache invalidation logic (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) in create/update/remove, so such an NPE would break those operations as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This PR is titled as caching support, but the getLoginPredicate change silently reclassifies every existing org-linked, non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC absent/false) IDP out of the login set for all providers, including the non-cached JPA path. Realms upgrading to this version see org-linked broker IdPs disappear from org login pages (orgs that relied on members-only brokers appearing) with no migration note, feature flag, or changelog entry; the change is shipped inside a 'caching' PR and reviewers/users will not expect a behavior change to login semantics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which means any org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` absent/false will no longer qualify as a “login” IDP wherever this predicate is used (not just the new Infinispan caching path). That is a cross-cutting behavioral change to login IDP eligibility, and the PR otherwise focuses on caching (`getForLogin` caching + invalidations), so the concern about unexpected semantic change is diff-grounded even if whether it’s “wrong” can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a cached IdentityProviderListQuery exists but lacks the current searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then addRevisioned with cache.getCurrentCounter(), which other cluster nodes can race with: a node that already fetched the old query between the invalidateObject and the addRevisioned re-caches against a stale snapshot, and the update-time invalidation skip (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returning early) then leaves the org-scoped stale list in place. In a multi-node cluster, a login-IDP update that the skip condition considers non-invalidation-worthy (e.g. alias-only change) coinciding with an org-scoped cache expansion can serve a stale org login list to users until some other operation invalidates the key; single-node tests like testCacheIDPForLogin cannot exercise this window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s login-cache entries store sets of IDP internal IDs per searchKey (organizationId), and `getForLogin` rehydrates current models via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`. The finding’s example (“alias-only change”) would not make the cached ID set stale because membership is unchanged and alias isn’t part of the cached set. Also, the claimed multi-node race relies on specific cluster semantics of `invalidateObject`, `addRevisioned`, and `getCurrentCounter()` that are not shown or verifiable from this diff alone. The diff does not demonstrate that an update deemed “non-invalidation-worthy” could change login eligibility or org scoping while skipping invalidation (it explicitly invalidates when predicate/org link changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On a cache hit the cached IDPs from session.identityProviders().getById(id) bypass createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (the initial load and the idp == null fallback) run the models through that wrapper, producing different IdentityProviderModel instances/behavior for the same login-page request depending on whether the login cache is warm. The very existence of the re-added `idp.isEnabled()` filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (comment: "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped") shows wrapped models diverge from raw ones; on cache hits the login page renders unwrapped cached models, so attributes the wrapper is supposed to contribute (organization-aware alias/config) silently differ between cache-miss and cache-hit renders, and the bean-level re-check only patches one of the divergences.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` implementation, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, and the `idp == null` fallback also maps through `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. But on a cache hit it reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly without explicitly applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` in this method. The finding’s claim that this *definitely* yields unwrapped models on cache hits is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone because `getById`’s implementation isn’t shown and may already perform the wrapping. Still, the diff does show an inconsistency in how models are produced between hit/miss paths, which is a concrete review issue worth addressing/clarifying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second-population branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) while the first-population branch uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), so the guard against installing a query over a concurrently-invalidated cache entry is bypassed in the multi-organization case. When one request is populating the cache for a second organizationId at the same moment another node/session invalidates the login cache (e.g. an IDP update), addRevisioned succeeds with a non-startup revision and stores a query built from pre-invalidation data, resurrecting stale login-IDP lists that the invalidation was supposed to clear; users see removed/disabled IDPs on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency in `getForLogin`: when `query == null` it does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but when extending an existing `IdentityProviderListQuery` for a new `searchKey` (i.e., `cached == null`) it does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. The finding’s broader claim about “bypassing the guard” and “resurrecting stale data under concurrent invalidation” depends on the (not-shown) semantics of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, and revision checks across nodes, so the concrete stale-data bug cannot be verified from this diff alone. However, the revision-parameter mismatch in two population paths is a specific, diff-grounded concern that could plausibly affect cache correctness under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before the cache-lookup branch, adding a guaranteed delegate (DB) read on every IDP removal even when the cache already holds the entry that used to satisfy the lookup. Every identity-provider removal across all realms pays an extra storage hit on a write path that previously could be served from cache; operators running hot IDP admin traffic see added DB load for information the cache branch already retrieves via the cached value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` / reading `realmCache`. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only called inside the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch, while the cache-valid path could rely on the cached entry to invalidate by internalId. The new unconditional delegate lookup is used for `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` (when invalid) and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (always), so every remove now performs that delegate read even if the cache contains the needed info. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/regression concern, not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is registered only from IDP create/update/remove in this provider; organization lifecycle changes that alter getForLogin results (organization removal unlinking IDPs, disabling an organization) do not register cacheKeyForLogin invalidations here, and the new login predicate's dependence on organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC makes those results sensitive to org-state. After an admin deletes or disables an organization whose linked public IDPs are cached in a login list query, login pages in that realm keep showing the stale org-linked IDPs until some unrelated IDP write triggers invalidation, letting users attempt brokering through a removed organization's IDP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new revisioned cache for `getForLogin` keyed by `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` and storing org-specific result sets inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` via `searchKey` (orgId or ""). Invalidation of these new login caches is only registered in this class from IDP `create`, `update` (conditional), and `remove` (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). The diff does not show any invalidation being triggered from organization lifecycle operations (e.g., org deletion/unlinking), so it’s a reasonable scope/architecture concern that org-side changes could leave `getForLogin` caches stale unless they flow through an IDP update/remove path. However, the finding’s mention of “disabling an organization” affecting the predicate is not evidenced here (the new predicate only checks `idp.getOrganizationId()` and `BROKER_PUBLIC`, not org enabled/disabled state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate clause idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) calls idp.getConfig() without a null guard, and applies the public check uniformly to all FetchMode values including ORG_ONLY, where members of the organization are expected to also see non-public broker entries. Any IdentityProviderModel implementation or deserialization path that leaves config null (getConfig() returning null) makes the shared getLoginPredicate throw NPE on every getForLogin call, breaking the login page; and org members lose their non-public organization brokers from the login page because ORG_ONLY results are filtered to public-only entries, contradicting the members-see-all-org-brokers behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new clause to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that unconditionally dereferences `idp.getConfig().get(...)` without any null guard, so if any `IdentityProviderModel` can ever have `getConfig()==null` this would NPE on `getForLogin` paths using this predicate. Also, the new condition (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || ...BROKER_PUBLIC`) is applied as part of the shared login predicate and is not parameterized by `FetchMode`, so it will exclude all non-public org-linked IDPs regardless of mode; whether that is correct for `ORG_ONLY` cannot be verified from this diff alone (the added test only covers public org-linked IDPs).
